scope:
Measure FP32 matrix-reduction error with exactly BF16-representable inputs.

Seed62 matches the earlier matrix probe. All native storage remains FP32;
Reduction mode varies dot length using prefixes of the same original data.
Active-terms mode retains one K2 matrix graph and changes only input values,
isolating the two products and reversing their order without recompilation.
This is a synthetic mechanism diagnostic, not learned-model attribution.
native_matrix_ops: %2 = "ttnn.matmul"(%0, %1) <{compute_config = #ttnn.device_compute_kernel_config<math_fidelity = hifi4, fp32_dest_acc_en = true>, transpose_a = false, transpose_b = false}> : (tensor<512x2xf32, #ttnn_layout3>, tensor<2x512xf32, #ttnn_layout4>) -> tensor<512x512xf32, #ttnn_layout2> loc(#loc3)
limits: Synthetic exact BF16-representable FP32-stored inputs, one K2 native matrix operation, no learned-model attribution. No SDK patch or measured internal instruction/rounding-point identification. Different cases change values but share the same shape, compiled graph and HiFi4/FP32 configuration.
finding: One shared native K2 FP32/HiFi4 matrix graph gives exact isolated products for both slots and either zeroed operand. Their CPU FP32 sum is bitwise the full CPU result, but the native two-active-term result has0.00013974 relative error. Reversing K leaves native output bitwise unchanged; positive products still have0.00011894 error and integer inputs are exact. Every value-only case avoids compilation/fallback, and fullK2 is bitwise the previous sweep. This demonstrates additional loss while the matrix path combines terms, without locating an internal rounding point or quantifying full-model contribution.
decision: Investigate accumulation/product-phase handling in native matrix kernels and BF16-source/FP32-output controls. Input representability alone cannot remove this measured loss; preserve exact isolated-product and unchanged-graph guards before trying full-model precision changes.
